questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I think it was a mix of it all - wanted to try something new, meet new people, study in a different way, explore a new city etc.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found a lot of places interesting to travel to - I ended up choosing a city I have been in before where they spoke english which I valued to be able to talk to the 'local' people living there. I ended up being very happy about valuing that ! I also chose Edinburgh because of the nature all around it, its beautiful architecture, people seeming friendly etc. Lots of good reason but also kind of randomly - to me, I think most cities can be interesting when you get to live and study in them:)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: very easy ! very good website of the University of Edinburgh and the study advisors were very easy to get in touch with. There was a looooot of information you needed to know what to sign, when to apply for specific things etc. which made me very overwhelmed at some point - but they were very helpful and quick to answer

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive much assistance but I got a lot of mails about possible assistance if needed ! there was a lot of both social events and opening hours at the study advisors place at the start

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was kind of difficult to find housing and I didn't find it until a couple of weeks before I went over there. Edinburgh is a expensive city and I don't know anyone who didn't pay a looooot in rent! I ended up paying 750 pounds pr month (6400 DKK) which seemed very average (at least among my friends). I found it through the website Spareroom which I can recommend ! I got it recommended as well as the place to find the cheapest rooms and it's my experience that spareroom was the easiest way to find a place !

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The same as I wrote above :) ALSO be patient ! A lot of the people renting out rooms for short terms renters publish an add about the room quite late - so don't just take the first and best!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is too expensive and difficult to get - buutttt I didn't meet anyone that didn't end up in a good room:)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was overwhelming but because everything was in english, it was quite easy to understand and get done when you took the time!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a lot with course registration, student card pictures, erasmus signing etc. before I went there - but I found the University of Edinburgh quite good to give the needed information and help

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know ... Many different ones - especially the student advisor was very visible with lots of opening hours ! I didn't really use it, so I don't know how helpful it was

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult with the pre-approval of University of Copenhagen (my home university) and then afterwards hoping there was space in the courses I wanted ... But I ended up with some of my first priorities !

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time, everything will work out :) and check your host university mail! I got a lot of information on that one

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had very interesting courses !!! I loved all three of them and the level was very similar to what I'm used to ! You can choose primarily just to have first year courses (which of course will make it a lot easier) which I didn't - which I guess have both pros and cons! I enjoyed learning from my courses but at the same time seeing the focus being a bit different from home, making something a bit easier for me

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I loved the way they did tutorials where we were only 10-12 in a class to discuss texts and arguments from the lectures ! Very scary at first, but I learned a lot from it and really enjoyed it at the end

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anthropology of Sex and Reproduction 
Social life and Climate change 
Gender, Sexualities and Health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would very much recommend anthropology of sex and reproduction (if you study anthropology or are interested in that sort of topic) !! it was very interesting, very cool professors and very important themes, analysis and focuses ! by far, my favourite course my whole degree so far

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used a lot of money on a travel card as I took the bus everyday for uni ! It was very worth it though ! I also didn't keep count of how much I spend so it's just guessing - I used most of my money on beers on pubs:)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh is an expensive city - very comparible with Copenhagen ! Some things are a bit cheaper, but it's close to the same

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there is A LOT of social events !! there is so many societies with different focuses that it was so overwhelming in the start. I would recommend people going to the Erasmus events in the start ! I didn't know about the ESN (Erasmus Student Network) until after the welcome week which was a shame. Other than that, there's so many societies so if you're interested in something, find a society to join!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I just wrote that above:) join ESN and societies ! but also take your time - you can always join or come by later in the semester

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I visited Isle of Skye - so so so beautiful if you love nature and hiking ! Other than that, I can recommend visiting Glasgow as well:) Glasgow is very easy with the train and bus, so that's a cute weekend activity from time to time

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy ! I loved it

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found that very difficult and I didn't get to know any scottish people at the university. It's a very international university, so I only talked to non-scottish people which was a bit of a shame...

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any, I think:) People is much more friendly and open than in Copenhagen which I enjoyed a lot

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open-ness with talking to strangers, being polite in the public, smiling etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
join ESN events from the start ! 
use the different university libraries, cafees etc. - they are so beautiful many of them
attend as much as possible (but don't take their talk about them taking attendance too seriously)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: nothing that I haven't already shared by now, I think

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting to know a lot of new people and exploring + living in a new city<3333

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: socialisation ! very overwhelming, but also so so worth it !

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
